q1.explanationZh: 男士说周末天气预报会晴朗暖和（bright and warm），大家更需要戴帽子遮挡阳光。A 错：最近有风，但现在已经停了；C 错：雨是之前下的，场地还没完全干。

q2.explanationZh: 女孩说妈妈要带她去书店参加 11 点的特别活动，男孩说自己也看到了海报，提议“我们就在那里见吧”（Let’s see each other there）。A 错：面包店只是妈妈要去的地方；B 错：公园是男孩上午待的地方，最后没有约在那里见。

q3.explanationZh: 女孩说房间刷成了浅蓝色，还会买配套的靠垫（cushions to match），已经在网上订好，明天到。B 错：台灯是她原来就有的；C 错：海报是原来墙上的，她只会挑最喜欢的重新贴上。

q4.explanationZh: 女孩在电影院排队买票时发现把钱包落在了公交车上，朋友帮她送来，她只好等着，所以错过了开头。A 错：她特意坐了早一班车，没有因为等车迟到；C 错：排队买票并不是她错过开头的原因。

q5.explanationZh: Danny 的哥哥在他家那条路尽头的餐馆上班，会开车经过他家门口，车里还能放下自行车，所以男孩坐车回家。A 错：他说想坐公交，但对方坚持送他；B 错：他的车灯摔坏了，不能骑车回家。

q6.explanationZh: 女孩说因为有优惠，这本书最后是 16 英镑（it was 16 pounds）。C 错：20 英镑是享受折扣需要的消费金额；A 错：7 英镑是她给自己买杂志花的钱。

q7.explanationZh: 女孩烧水时接到朋友电话，回到自己房间帮朋友查东西，再回来泡茶时手机已经不在身上了，所以手机在她卧室里。C 错：她在外面桌边时手机还在，后来带进了屋；B 错：在厨房时手机还在身上，后来才带去了卧室。

q8.explanationZh: 女孩说教练想尽办法让她在没信心的时候也对自己感觉良好，她觉得这一点很重要，说明她很感激教练的支持。A 错：别人最后都上了最高的跳台，她没有；C 错：她一开始就知道会很难，并不感到意外。

q9.explanationZh: 男孩说他们打算坐火车去，电影开始前半小时就能到，并邀请 Megan 一起坐车（Why not come with us），是在建议她怎样去电影院。A 错：没有提醒她别迟到；C 错：他道歉是因为她想看的电影没有上映，不是因为给错了信息。

q10.explanationZh: 女孩说她担心的不是天气，而是自己能不能让船走直线、不撞到湖上的其他东西——也就是担心控制不好船。B 错：她明确说大风不是她担心的事（that’s not what’s bothering me）；A 错：她没有说不知道要做什么。

q11.explanationZh: 男孩说完全没想到最后那一幕，女孩也说本以为知道结局，直到最后 5 分钟才发现不对——两人都觉得结局出人意料。A 错：只有女孩觉得男主角演得好，男孩觉得一般；C 错：女孩喜欢发电站的场景，男孩却不明白为什么选那里。

q12.explanationZh: 男孩说前排的观众一直上蹦下跳，他有时看不见舞台，这让演出有点扫兴——他不喜欢的是观众的行为。B 错：嫌声音太大的是女孩，男孩说他不介意；C 错：他说乐队演了所有热门歌曲，只可惜时间太短。

q13.explanationZh: 男孩说一直要在大门口排队，很烦人；女孩说她更喜欢安静一点——两人都觉得那里人太多。B 错：女孩认为是他们自己没看仔细，不是指引不清楚；C 错：女孩觉得太热，男孩却喜欢热天。

q14.explanationZh: 老师说 12 世纪的一场大火之后，城堡大部分都要重建。11 世纪是最早建造的时间，13 世纪是重建的时间，都不是被毁的时间。

q15.explanationZh: 当时人们一般用木头盖房子，但这座城堡是用石头建的，说明它很重要。wood（木头）和 earth（泥土）是其他建筑常用的材料。

q16.explanationZh: 据说那位富有的女人把她的金币藏在一个秘密的地方。画像里的戒指和项链只是她戴的首饰，不是藏起来的东西。

q17.explanationZh: 老师让学生在花园里想象这片土地以前是一个农场，当时用来为城堡里的人提供食物。picnic area 和 garden 是现在的样子。

q18.explanationZh: 午饭后会有一个小测验（quiz），看谁记住的参观内容最多。看电影是一到城堡就做的事，不是下午的活动。

q19.explanationZh: 城堡最后的主人叫 William Haisworth，录音中逐个字母拼出 H-A-I-S-W-O-R-T-H，注意拼写。

q20.explanationZh: 一位报社记者来采访她，并建议她去当体育节目主持人，她就下定了决心。A 错：是她在大学训练女子足球队，并不是教练鼓励她；C 错：参观电视台是她做出决定之后的事。

q21.explanationZh: Maria 说很多人都梦想在电视上做体育节目，所以工作竞争非常激烈。B 错：她说有培训课程，只是很贵；C 错：她说直播时压力很大，但没有说要证明自己反应快。

q22.explanationZh: 她第一次上直播前很紧张，去跑了很长一段步，让自己平静下来。A 错：她是直播之后才看自己的录像，而且觉得很不自在；C 错：别人让她要自信，但她说自己就是不敢相信，并不是靠听建议准备的。

q23.explanationZh: 她说自己最担心的是采访时突然忘了下一个要问的问题，因为对话一变，想好的东西就会忘掉。C 错：她说有的主持人会念错长名字，但她没有出过这种错；B 错：她是提问的人，不用回答问题。

q24.explanationZh: 她说会走遍全国，亲自尝试这些新运动（having a go at some of these activities）。A 错：家乡只是她想到这个点子的地方；B 错：他们会拍青少年运动，但没有说要采访年轻体育明星。

q25.explanationZh: 她建议了解多种运动，不要只想着电视，可以去当地体育赛事找采访机会，或者到报社、电台找工作——也就是获得各种各样的经验。B 错：她说你不知道最后会报道什么运动，所以不要只学一种；C 错：她说要观察专家怎么做，没有说向他们求助。

content.v: Test Three. There are four parts to the test. You will hear each part twice. We will now stop for a moment. Please ask any questions now because you must not speak during the test.
Now open your question papers and look at Part One.
For each question, choose the correct answer. Look at question one.
One. What will the weather be like at the weekend?

OK, everyone. About the cricket match at the weekend. Fortunately, it won’t be as wet on the ground as we’d expected since we’ve had some wind lately … though this has stopped now. It wasn’t enough to really dry the field out from all that rain, so the conditions won’t be great for playing. Anyway, you’re more likely to need your caps to protect your eyes, as it’s going to be bright and warm, according to the forecast. That’ll be better for the ground.
Two. Where will the two friends meet tomorrow?
Can we still meet tomorrow? I’ll be in the park all morning.
Well, I’m going to town with my mum – she says she wants to go to the bakers, and there’s a special event she wants to take me to at the bookshop at 11, but I’ll come straight afterwards.
Oh – I saw a poster for that. It sounds really interesting! Let’s see each other there. It’s not far from the park, and my parents were actually encouraging me to go to it.
OK. That sounds like a plan.
Three. What is the girl getting for her bedroom?
Have you finished painting your room?
Yes – we finished last night. I went for blue in the end. I chose a really nice pale colour, and I’ll have cushions to match.
Nice! That’s a good idea – and you can change them easily when you want things to look different.

Exactly. I ordered some online – they’ll arrive tomorrow. Everything looked so dark before, even with that lamp of mine in the corner. Maybe it was all my posters on the wall. I’ll put some back up, but just my favourites!
Four. Why did the girl miss the start of the film?
How was the film?
Good – although I didn’t see the start!
Oh dear! Was the bus late again?

Oh, it always is, so I made sure I got an earlier one. No, when I was waiting in the cinema queue for my ticket, I realised I’d left my purse on the bus. Luckily a friend saw it there. She called me and brought it to the cinema, so I had to wait, which meant missing the beginning.
Oh dear!
I know.
Five. How will the boy get home?

Hi Mum, I just wanted to let you know I’ll be home a bit late. I was cycling to Danny’s after school and my light fell off and broke! But Danny’s brother works in the restaurant at the end of our road, so he drives right past our door. He’s got enough room to put my bike in the boot too. I said I’d get the bus, but he insisted. Anyway – I’ll see you later!
Six. How much did the girl pay for the book?
I got that book Jack wanted for his birthday.
Oh, that’s great. He’ll be pleased.
Yeah, I hope so, it was quite expensive. Paying so much for a book is unusual for me!
Well, it’s his birthday, after all. And wasn’t there a special offer on at the bookshop? Something like if you spend over 20 pounds you get a discount?
That’s right – so it was 16 pounds, and I got some magazines for myself for 7 pounds as well. I think Jack’ll be happy anyway!
Seven. Where is the girl’s phone?
Dad, have you seen my phone? I’m sure I had it when we were sitting round the table outside earlier today.
Sorry, no. But didn’t you take it with you when you went back in to make tea for me and Mum?

Good point, you’re right. And when I was waiting for the water to boil, a friend called me about some homework. I had to go to my room and check something for her, but I didn’t have the phone when I came back to make the tea.
Mystery solved.
That is the end of Part One.
Now look at Part Two. For each question, choose the correct answer.
Eight. You will hear a girl talking to a friend about a diving course she did.
How was the course, Jo?

My diving course? Great, thanks. When I started I was scared to even jump in the deep end of the pool to be honest, so I knew it’d be hard! Some of the other people were using the highest diving board by the end – not me. I know I’ve still got a lot to learn, but that’s OK. I’ve even signed up for another course!
You enjoyed it then.
Yeah. The instructor did everything possible to make me feel good about myself when I wasn’t feeling too positive! Which is really important.
Nine. You will hear a boy talking to a friend about a trip to the cinema.
Hello Megan, are you still OK to come with us to the cinema on Sunday?
Yeah – I’m looking forward to it!
I’m really glad you can still come. Sorry the film you wanted to see isn’t on.
Oh, that’s fine – this one sounds cool anyway.

That’s good. Well, we’re going to get the train there – there’s one that gets to town about half an hour before the film, which gives us plenty of time to get tickets and snacks. Why not come with us, then we’ll arrive together?
Thanks, but actually I’ll be in town already. So I’ll see you there.
Ten. You will hear two friends talking about a sailing lesson they’re going to have.
I’m really looking forward to learning to sail with an instructor on Saturday. Are you?
Yes and no. It’s going to be really windy on Saturday afternoon – I saw the forecast but, of course, you need wind for sailing.
Or else we won’t actually get anywhere.
I know – that’s not what’s bothering me. It’s more whether I’ll be able to keep sailing in a straight line without hitting anything else on the lake! How do you avoid that?
I don’t know but we’ll find out.
I suppose we won’t do anything too challenging as it’s our first lesson.
No.
Eleven. You will hear two friends talking about a film.
What did you think of the film?
I liked it – I thought the main actor was fantastic – but he’s one of my favourites, so I like whatever he’s in!
He was OK. I wonder if this was the right sort of film for him though … Anyway, I really didn’t expect that final scene, did you?
I was sure I knew exactly what was going to happen – until the last 5 minutes! I wonder where it was filmed? Using that power station really added something to the atmosphere.
I didn’t get that – why a power station? But the beach scene was amazing.
Twelve. You will hear two friends talking about a concert.
Did you go to see the band BlueDay, Billy?
Yeah – my dad got tickets! Our seats were quite far back, not right near the speakers like when you’re in the ones at the front.
I hate it if it’s too loud.

I don’t mind it. Everyone in the rows in front was jumping up and down though, so I couldn’t always see, which spoilt it a little. But the band played all their biggest hits. It was all over so quickly. It’s a shame they couldn’t go on for longer, but I hope I can go and see them again some time.
Thirteen. You will hear two friends talking about a walk they went on.
What a great walk!
Yes, but the heat was a bit much for me!
Oh, I like it when it’s hot. The route was complicated, though, and the directions we were using weren’t that great.
I think that was because we didn’t follow them properly.
Well, maybe. But we missed a really important turning!
I think it was us not looking carefully. And there were people around to ask all over the place.
True. Although I found having to wait in queues to go through the gates all the time annoying.
Mmm, I prefer more peace and quiet.
That is the end of Part Two.
Now look at Part Three.
For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Write one or two words or a number or a date or a time. Look at questions 14 to 19 now. You have 20 seconds.
You will hear a history teacher telling some students about a castle they will visit.
OK everybody. We’re going on a class trip to Lea Castle next week so I’d like to tell you a bit about the castle.

The oldest parts of it were built in the 11th century, a time when there were lots of battles in the area. But following a fire in the 12th century, most of it had to be built again. This didn’t happen until the 13th century.

As you know, people generally made their buildings from wood – after all, much of the area is covered in trees even now. Building with stone wasn’t easy, so the fact it was used here shows how important this castle was. It was much stronger than buildings made using earth, which was also common back then.

You’ll be interested to hear something valuable might be hidden somewhere in the castle. There’s a story about a rich woman who lived there. Look out for pictures of her around the castle – she’s wearing expensive rings and necklaces in the paintings. It’s believed she put her gold coins in a secret place. Nobody knows where!

When we’ve finished in the castle, we’ll go outside to the picnic area. While we’re there, enjoying the castle’s beautiful garden, try and imagine the land as a farm. That’s how it was used to provide food for people in the castle.

Finally, after lunch, there’ll be a quiz to see who in the class remembers most about what you saw during the tour. So pay attention to the guide, and also remember to make notes during the film you’ll see when we first arrive.

The last owner of the castle was an interesting man and I’d like you to find out something about him for homework. His name was William Haisworth. That’s H-A-I-S-W-O-R-T-H. You can look up some information online.
That is the end of Part Three.
Now look at Part Four. For each question, choose the correct answer.
Look at questions 20 to 25 now. You have 45 seconds.
You will hear an interview with a TV sports presenter called Maria Dalton.
Today I’m interviewing Maria Dalton, who works as a TV sports presenter.
Hello.
What made you become a sports presenter?

I’ve always loved sports – doing things like training the women’s football team at college. People said I gave very clear instructions. A guy who worked on a newspaper came to ask me questions for an article he was writing, and he suggested I’d make a good sports presenter. I made up my mind I’d like to try it so I did a tour of a television studio to find out what it was like.
I see! Is the profession hard to get into?

Well, it’s common to dream of working in sport on TV, so that means strong competition for jobs. There are courses you can do, though they’re quite expensive. When you’re presenting a sports programme on live TV, it’s stressful in the studio with busy people all around you – it’s not just sitting in front of a camera!
How did you prepare for your first time on live TV?

I was nervous! Everyone kept saying I should feel confident because I deserved the job, but I just couldn’t believe it was happening! I went for a long run, which made me feel calmer. Afterwards, I felt really uncomfortable seeing the recording of myself, although I’m used to it now.
So what do you worry about when you’re on TV?

There’s always something! For me, it’s suddenly not knowing what I’d planned to ask next when I’m talking to sportspeople. I have ideas written down, but sometimes a conversation changes, and things go out of my head. Some presenters make mistakes when they’re trying to say long names and things, but that hasn’t happened to me.
I hear you’re doing a new TV programme soon.

Yes, I’m so excited. I got the idea from watching kids in my hometown doing amazing new sports like underwater basketball. So I’m going around the country, having a go at some of these activities. And we’ll film teenagers doing their sports – there may be some future champions!
Do you have advice for people interested in sports journalism?

Well, although everyone has favourite sports they can talk about for hours, you never know what you’ll end up covering, so knowledge about a variety is important. And just don’t think about TV. Look for interview opportunities at local sports events, or ask about positions in newspapers or radio. And watch what the experts in the profession do.
Thanks Maria!
Thank you.
That is the end of Part Four.
You now have six minutes to write your answers on the answer sheet.
You have one more minute.
That is the end of the test.
